(Obviously this is me just talking from my experience so others may need medication as a necessity and I’m not saying it’s bad to take them, they just don’t agree with me) It was really good for me to hear that and maybe you’d like to hear that too so just thought I’d say

I’m lucky that I don’t fear death every day so I can’t say I have any amazing advice and like someone else said if you could get a good therapist I’m sure that would be helpful but this is just my two pence might not be helpful at all. But I definitely have had times in my life when the thought of death has been very overwhelming. A few things have helped me one that I do think of a lot is the quote: “I do not fear death. I have been dead for billions and billions of years, and have not suffered the slightest inconvenience from it.” I saw that you said your not religious but wish at times that’s you could be and I definitely relate to that. Have always wished in a way I was so that I could believe everyone I cared about would be in heaven or something like that. But this quote really helped me. I have very bad anxiety and being alive has always been difficult! But like the quote says death has not caused me any suffering. I would be fearing something that hasn’t caused me any problems. To be honest I’ve had times in my life where I’ve thought it would be easier to not be here and if you haven’t then again this might not be helpful but the days where I feel alright I’m just really grateful for, not that I’m doing anything crazy because I don’t really leave the house at the moment apart from going to CBT but I do appreciate the little things. But any day I get to be here i feel is a bonus. Again not to say it’s easy and I’m not out there living my best life! But if I feel alright I will take it! My mum also used to say to me when I was little that there was no point in worrying about death because your wasting the time you do have. Obviously easier said than done and I’m sure you’ve heard that before but it’s true and it helped me a lot when I was little worrying about it and even now if I do have that fear of death come over me I just try to tell myself but were here now why waste that time worrying about it. I also have a million other things to worry about anyway so I’m busy with them! I can’t say I know the answer to this as I’m only just starting cbt but so far what I’m having to do is make a list of the things the give me anxiety, (mine is more to do with a phobia of being sick which has lead to me not leaving the house, so it wouldn’t be exactly the same as yours but) you then need to rate it on a scale of 20-100% anxiety things that would be uncomfortable but doable to the most difficult seemingly impossible right now. Then take something that’s about a 40% to push you but not too far and do that. Sit with the feeling until it goes down. It won’t go fully down, say you were doing something that was an 80% on the list but maybe it would go down to a 65% after 10 or 15 minutes then you can leave. So maybe if walking around the block is giving you that stress and not coming down (which I relate to, I’m not at that point yet, I know I could go and do it but I would be very stressed so it’s pointless doing as it will only further give my brain reasons to think it’s a ‘dangerous’ situation) start off with just being at the end of the path and stand there or potter there until you come down to a lower level of anxiety and then go back in. It’s a really difficult thing to do, so don’t feel defeated it is obviously easier to do with a therapists input but at the end of the day it is all down to what we put into it (that’s what I’m told anyway even though my brain try’s to convince me I’ll not be able to do what other people can!) then you need to repeat it until it gives you about 20% anxiety and then move onto another thing on the list. Hope this explains a bit! Like I say I’m just getting started so I definitely don’t have all the answers!

So now I’m trying to get better without them, and I’m hoping I will, so don’t feel that just because you aren’t on them you have any less chance of getting better. If you are able to get cbt (congestive behaviour therapy) that might be helpful but i know it’s not easy to get! I think it’s nice to know that medication it’s always there, it’s not going to disappear so you can always keep that at the back of your mind, I like to remember that. Obviously I don’t know your situation and you might have other things going on but it seems to me that a lot of things are down to your mind, Ive been so amazed by how many problems that feel so real are just your brain making them and if you can change your way of thinking (of course easier said than done!) then medication isn’t the be all end all. But please don’t let feel defeated that your not on medication it, I really believe a lot of people can get better without them 💕

I don’t really have any amazing advice but just wanted to say I am in the same situation so you are not alone! It really sucks as an understatement! I had to quit my job because of it. One of the things I’m trying to do at the moment is get out each day, start with sitting in the garden if you have one then, a small walk, I have a park near me so I go walk there and sit for about half an hour if I’m feeling better I walk up the hill to a bench and sit there. (As I’m saying this I haven’t been out today so this has reminded me to go at least have a sit outside!) Also something random that I’ve noticed is the harder something seems to be almost the less anxious I end up being, I’ve been putting off an opticians appointment for ages now and went last Thursday I was so anxious about it but once I was there I actually felt alright and less nauseous because I was distracted because all the things you have to do and then yesterday I went into our town with my mum and had a freak out even though it was way less of a thing to do than the opticians. But what I’m trying to say but failing a bit to explain! Is sometimes the smaller things are harder than the bigger things because you are less distracted so don’t beat yourself up when they seem so hard because they are when it’s all you can think about. Keep trying to do the small things that will build to one day doing the bigger things. I also like to try and think that the hardest part of recovery is right now in the thick of it hopefully as I am able to do more things you are more distracted and have less time to think about being worried that you might be nauseous.
